title: audit-surface-and-buyer-rebuttals-for-onprem-control-plane
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical go-to-market note aimed at sellers, solutions engineers, and product marketers who need crisp language to explain Redwood’s on-prem / VPC control plane options to regulated buyers. Focus is audit surface (what auditors ask about), concrete rebuttals to common objections, and competitive differentiators. This is intentionally tactical — use these lines in proposals, call scripts, and the vendor-security appendix of RFP responses.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Regulated buyers care about two things: where control and telemetry live (control plane vs data plane) and who holds the keys/audit logs.
- Positioning: offer a single coherent message: "Customer-owned data path; optional managed control plane that can be deployed in-customer (VPC or on-prem) or minimized to a relay-only service with no persisted customer data."
- Primary rebuttal themes: minimize surface area, provide clear contractual and technical controls, and map directly to typical auditor questions (data residency, key management, change control, logging).

Common buyer objections and suggested responses (sales script style):
1) "We can't allow any third-party control plane in our network — it violates policy."
   - Rebuttal: "We get that. We support two proven options: (A) Self-hosted control plane (customer deploys Redwood control plane containers in their VPC/on-prem; we provide an ops bundle and runbook), or (B) Relay-only managed control plane where all model payloads and artifacts are kept in your environment and the control plane only signals job state (no persisted payloads). We can include an attestation in the SOW that confirms no customer payloads are stored by the managed control plane."
   - Tech call note: show architecture diagram that highlights token-by-token processing in the compute plane isolated to the customer's subnet.

2) "How do we prove data never left our environment?"
   - Rebuttal: "We provide: (1) network diagrams and flow logs, (2) packet capture guidance for a customer validation window, (3) configurable egress-only NAT rules we recommend for the control plane, and (4) runtime telemetry that can be forwarded to your SIEM (we don't store payloads in the managed control plane unless the customer opts in)."

3) "We require KMS/HSM integration and key ownership."
   - Rebuttal: "Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations or on-prem HSMs. For Private deployments we can enforce envelope encryption where keys never leave your KMS and Redwood never holds plaintext or key material. Add this to the standard security appendix."

4) "What about patching and SBOMs?"
   - Rebuttal: "We deliver SBOMs and weekly CVE summaries for the control plane components. For self-hosted installs, we provide a support-backed patch schedule and optional concierge patching assistance under an enterprise SLA."

5) "FedRAMP / IL4 / other certifications?"
   - Rebuttal: "Certification needs dictate deployment model. For FedRAMP/IL4 customers we recommend a fully private control plane and restricted compute pools; we will work with your cloud integrator and provide the necessary artifacts (SSP elements, control mappings). Note: achieving a specific certification requires customer collaboration; we provide the platform and artifacts, not the certification itself."

Audit surface checklist (what auditors will ask) — maps to how sellers should respond:
- Data flow diagram: Provide a clear diagram showing control plane vs data plane, egress points, and controls for telemetry. (Deliverable: put in appendix of proposal.)
- Key custody: Who manages KMS? Provide exact KMS ARNs and proof-of-integration.
- Logging and retention: Show where logs are stored, retention settings, and who has access. Offer optional forwarding to customer SIEM.
- Change control: Provide Git/PR audit trail for any code pushed to the control plane and a release checklist. Include configuration drift policies.
- Incident response: Provide an incident playbook sample and SOC contact info.
- SBOM and patch cadence: Provide SBOM, CVE backlog, and patch SLAs.

Recommended control-plane language (short, shareable lines):
- "Customer-owned compute and storage for model inference; control plane can be run in-customer or configured as a relay-only managed service with no persisted customer payloads."
- "Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — we never see plaintext when configured."
- "Full logging and SIEM integration; retention controlled by the customer."
- "Contractual SOW option for air-gapped or on-prem installs with assisted delivery and runbooks."

Competitive callouts (how to differentiate vs cloud LLM APIs and self-hosted runtimes):
- Against public LLM APIs (e.g., large cloud vendors): emphasize predictable performance (Dedicated pools), auditability, and deployment options that meet regulatory constraints. Cloud APIs = simple but often unacceptable for regulated customers because of control plane/data plane ambiguity.
- Against self-hosted open-source runtimes: emphasize operational maturity — we provide SRE-runbooks, tested production packaging, and prebuilt CVE/SBOM artifacts. Self-hosting alone often fails audits because it lacks formal change control and vendor-backed acceptance testing.
- Against specialized inference vendors that insist on a single managed control plane: call out our flexible deployment matrix (managed, relay-only, self-hosted) and our contractual commitments around data non-persistence for managed relay modes.

Proposal appendix snippets (copy-paste ready):
- "Control Plane options: (A) Managed (hosted) — best for speed to market and non-regulated teams; (B) Managed relay-only — control plane orchestrates but does not persist customer data; (C) Customer-deployed control plane — vendor-provided images + runbook; Redwood provides installation support and optional ongoing patching under an Enterprise SOW."
- "KMS and Key Custody: Customer will provide and manage encryption keys via [cloud KMS / on-prem HSM]. Redwood will operate under envelope encryption and will not store key material in plaintext."
- "Audit Artifacts: At delivery we will provide network diagrams, SBOM, CVE report, and log export playbook. Additional compliance artifacts (e.g., SSP excerpts) available via signed NDA and SOW."

Suggested simple KPI frame for sales conversations:
- Security: "Zero customer payload persistence in relay mode (attested)."
- Time-to-production: "Private deployment baseline: 4–8 weeks for VPC install with standard onboarding; air-gap installs vary."
- Latency: "Dedicated pools target X ms p50 for long-sequence workloads (include benchmark link)."
- Ops burden: "Customer-managed control plane reduces vendor-managed footprint but shifts patch responsibility; Redwood offers optional managed patching."

Next steps for product + sales enablement (owner: Aisha):
- Create two one-pagers: (1) 'Control plane options one-pager' and (2) 'Auditor artifact checklist' (Due: 2024-11-20).
- Build an 'attestation' template legal can sign for relay-only mode (owner: Legal).
- Add a short sample network diagram (PNG) to the sales deck and link it in the SFX playbook (owner: Design/SE).
- Record a 15-minute SE training that walks through objections above and demo of KMS integration (owner: Solutions Engineering).

Notes and open questions: 
- Need legal to confirm acceptable wording for "we will not persist customer payloads" — limited to 'to the best of our technical controls' vs absolute warranty.
- Need an internal checklist to prove relay-only control plane does not leak metadata (time-to-live for entries, queue sizing).
- Consider a small 'audit concierge' package for large deals to accelerate certification evidence requests.

Appendix: Example audit artifact list (deliverables):
- Network/data flow diagrams (pdf)
- SBOM for control plane components (csv/pdf)
- KMS integration guide and example ARNs (md)
- Log export playbook + SIEM connector config (md)
notes: Working doc for sales and product; iterations expected. Do not publish externally without Legal review.
